messages:
jess: Quick sync — we need a concrete approval + rollout lifecycle for high-impact runtime toggles (routing weights, quota floors, fast-path flags). Problem: a few recent flips caused unexpected routing shifts and token cost spikes. Proposal below, please reaction or pushback.

sam: +1 on having stricter controls. can you sketch API + console UX?

jess: Sketch: 1) classification: low/medium/high by expected traffic impact (heuristic: traffic delta + token delta). 2) approvals: high requires 2 approvers (one eng-platform, one product/owner). 3) rollout plan: auto-canary -> staged percent increases with time windows (e.g., 1% for 10m, 10% for 30m, 50% for 2h). 4) telemetry gates: p95 latency, error-rate, token-cost-percent-change thresholds. 5) auto-pause & rollback if gates fail. 6) dry-run mode + preview diff showing projected token delta and routes affected.

maria: Two questions: a) who are approvers? we need a group mapping so we don't block during timezones. b) approvals + long manual waits will slow urgent fixes. can we have an 'on-call fast-track' that still logs everything and requires post-approval?

devon: For telemetry gates we should plug into existing eval infra. Example gate hook (pseudo):
```
POST /rollouts/{id}/evaluate
{
  "window": "10m",
  "checks": ["p95_latency < 200ms", "error_rate < 0.5%", "token_cost_change < 15%"]
}
```
If any check fails, rollout pauses and an automated rollback job runs.

lee: UI notes: show the projected token delta as a single number (tokens/hour) and a small sparkline of recent token usage, plus the list of routes that will change weight. Also add a safety slider: max percent-per-step (default 10%). We should also show who the approvers are (group names) and ETA for manual approvals.

ana: permission scoping: high-impact flags must only be creatable by a role with 'critical-config:write'. Also require an audit entry tied to KMS key-id if the change touches encrypted config. We should include a tamper-evident audit id in the rollout metadata.

sam: On API surface, I suggest a single endpoint to create a rollout object that contains the plan and gates so the console + CLI + API are consistent. Example body: 
```
{
  "flag": "route_priority_v2",
  "classification": "high",
  "steps": [{"pct":1,"duration":"10m"},{"pct":10,"duration":"30m"}],
  "gates": [{"metric":"p95_latency","threshold":200},{"metric":"error_rate","threshold":0.005}],
  "approvers_required":2
}
```
Then `POST /rollouts` returns rollout-id. Approvals are `POST /rollouts/{id}/approve` and can be batched.

maria: Can we make approvals asynchronous so the rollout can still progress through auto-stepped phases until it hits a manual-only phase? e.g., auto 1%->10% but require manual for >50%?

jess: I like that. Default policy: auto until 25%, manual if >25% for high classification. Fast-track binder for on-call (time-limited override) with email+slack audit.

devon: Also suggest a secondary telemetry check that runs synthetic traffic tests (small loadbench) to validate routing changes don't hit edge-case nodes. Could be optional but useful for multi-tenant isolated pools.

ops-bot: :information_source: runbook reminder: For high-impact rollouts, trigger the 'rollout-watch' channel and create an incident if rollback occurs. Reference: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/rollout-watch

lee: UX corner case: if a rollout is paused mid-step by the gate, console should surface the failing metric, show last good checkpoint, and provide 1-click rollback -> create a rollback job with prefilled params. Also surface estimated cost refunds (if applicable).

ana: compliance note: we need to retain approvals + audit trail for 365 days for enterprise customers. Capture approver SAML id and ip.

infra-bot: :robot_face: New rollout schema registered in staging: rollout_v2. Tests: unit + e2e queued. CI job: rollout-schema-test-42.

sam: one more API nit: add `dry_run=true` mode that runs the gate checks on expected traffic via sampling (shadow routing) but doesn't change config. Useful for predicting regressions.

jess: Action items: 1) @sam draft API spec for rollout_v2 (include dry_run and fast-track flag) by EOD tomorrow. 2) @lee produce console mockups (preview diff + approver flow) by Tue. 3) @devon wire a prototype gate call to eval infra and share sample payload. 4) @maria + @ana define approver groups + compliance retention.

maria: ack. I'll start mapping approvers and timezone coverage.

devon: I'll take the gate prototype.

lee: on it for mocks.

jess: thanks all. If anyone sees an obvious security hole (elevated fast-track abuse, audit gaps) call it out here. otherwise we'll spin an RFC and mark as 'required for next release'. :thumbsup:
